endorsements.quote: First, CPD must prioritize AI literacy as a foundational professional skill.
This includes the ability to interrogate models effectively, verify AI-generated evidence, recognize hallucinations, and interpret model explanations.

CPD must support the development of meta-competencies such as disagreement negotiation (how clinicians respond when AI contradicts them), escalation pathways, and collaborative sense-making using shared digital tools.

unlisted_practices: Design continuing professional development to promote shared mental models of AI tools across nurses, physicians, pharmacists, and other health professionals.
Help clinicians interpret AI-generated personal analytics constructively, avoid over-reliance on algorithmic judgment, and maintain autonomy and moral agency.
Redesign continuing professional development systems with dynamic curricula, continuous assessment, real-time feedback, and personalized learning trajectories.
Reinforce clinicians' moral agency and ultimate accountability for clinical actions through continuing professional development as AI participates in clinical judgments.
Recalibrate continuing professional development from retention of biomedical facts toward formulating effective questions and evaluating the validity of AI-generated information.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual/perspective paper examining how AI transforms health professional competence and continuous professional development, providing frameworks and educational/governance perspectives rather than an empirical study.
